audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $637.999 million, or $14.49 per diluted share; required operating-cash portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments to equity value even though some may be required to support seasonal working capital and the owner-earnings stream.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company relies on excess operating cash flows, which are largely generated in Fall, to fund operations throughout the fiscal year and to reinvest in the business to support future growth.
audit_findings.explanation: The full $637.999 million addition is demonstrated, but the amount actually required for operations is unresolved. The maximum exposure exceeds the base-case cushion over market price: base equity value exceeds market capitalization by approximately $516.1 million, or $11.73 per share. Thus an operating-cash requirement above that amount would reverse the base case's modest premium to the market price.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum cash and short-term investments required across the full seasonal cycle, exclude restricted or unavailable balances, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: A one-time litigation benefit appears embedded in the latest-actual anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $38.574 million pre-tax and $28.882 million after tax, equal to 6.3% of the $460.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring settlement increased fiscal-2025 earnings included in the annual owner-earnings anchor and is consequently propagated through forecast owner earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The settlement resulted in a $ 39 million net benefit recorded in the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive Income for Fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization error unless an undocumented reversal exists. The filing expressly removes $28.882 million after tax from adjusted fiscal-2025 net income, while the supplied valuation discloses no corresponding owner-earnings adjustment. A 6.3% anchor distortion is material given the base value is only 7.8% above the market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the owner-earnings schedule, remove the $28.882 million after-tax settlement benefit from the fiscal-2025 anchor unless already reversed elsewhere, and rerun all scenarios and the margin-of-safety threshold.

audit_findings.title: Known post-anchor tariff pressure may invalidate immediate growth assumptions
audit_findings.magnitude: filed fiscal-2026 estimate of $40 million pre-tax, equal to 8.7% of the $460.3 million anchor; remaining effect after first-half actuals unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental tariffs reduce forecast operating profit and after-tax owner earnings; omitting the initial reset causes growth to begin from an overstated recurring earnings level.
audit_findings.evidence: Assuming the estimated impact from the tariffs on goods imported into the U.S., including the impact of a 15% tariff on all U.S. imports (which, for purposes of our outlook, is expected to apply beginning February 24, 2026, and to remain in effect for the entirety of Fiscal 2026), and factoring in certain planned mitigation strategies, we expect to incur approximately $40 million of incremental impact compared to Fiscal 2025, or approximately 70 basis points as a percentage of net sales, which would negatively impact our operating income during Fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The fiscal-2025 anchor already contains $90 million of tariff expense, but management subsequently forecast another $40 million of fiscal-2026 pressure after planned mitigation. First-half fiscal-2026 results include ongoing tariffs and substantial one-time tariff refunds, so the current residual cannot be established from the supplied record. Nevertheless, the filed estimate is large enough relative to the anchor and the narrow base-case premium to require an explicit year-one treatment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile fiscal-2026 year-to-date owner earnings to ongoing tariff expense, exclude the $100 million recognized refund and the subsequent $14 million refund from recurring earnings, estimate the remaining after-tax fiscal-2026 burden without double-counting mitigation, and rerun the forecast with an explicit first-year reset.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter conflicts with an announced APAC strategic review
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.281 million first-half fiscal-2026 operating loss, $90.666 million first-half sales, and $107.831 million of APAC long-lived assets and intellectual property; transaction effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A divestiture, closure, partnership, or restructuring could alter recurring owner earnings, capital expenditure, working capital, disposal proceeds, stranded costs, and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to the end of Fiscal 2025, the Company announced a review of strategic alternatives for the APAC region.
audit_findings.explanation: The strategic review is confirmed, but no selected alternative, probability, consideration, exit cost, lease treatment, or stranded-cost estimate is supplied. APAC is currently loss-making but small relative to the consolidated business, so eliminating its losses could increase value while restructuring costs or stranded overhead could reduce it. The record cannot establish the net materiality or direction of a transaction.
audit_findings.action: Review developments through the valuation date and obtain any board-approved plan, transaction terms, disposal or closure estimates, lease obligations, tax effects, and stranded-cost analysis; then rerun the perimeter if an outcome is sufficiently probable.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be mixed with consolidated add-backs and cash subject to NCI
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.804 million of first-half fiscal-2026 NCI income, annualized to $5.608 million or 1.2% of the $460.3 million anchor; $15.141 million NCI equity, or 0.2% of $7.105 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Using parent-attributable net income with wholly consolidated depreciation, capital expenditures, working-capital changes, or cash would include minority-owned economics in owner earnings or the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is deemed to be the primary beneficiary of these VIEs; therefore, the Company has consolidated the operating results, assets and liabilities of these VIEs, with the noncontrolling interests’ (“NCI”) portions of net income presented as net income attributable to NCI on the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive Income and the NCI portion of stockholders’ equity presented as NCI on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: A consistency issue remains possible, but the currently filed NCI amounts are too small to change the valuation conclusion. Annualized NCI income is approximately 1.2% of the anchor, and NCI equity is approximately 0.2% of base equity value. These scales are well below the $516.1 million base-value cushion over market capitalization.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each owner-earnings component and bridge asset to the parent-common claim and allocate VIE cash flows and cash consistently; correct any mismatch in the next model refresh.

audit_findings.title: Mandatory advancement of a former executive's defense costs is an open-ended cash claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued future advancement payments, net of insurance or reimbursement, would reduce future owner earnings or the equity bridge; recurring legal expense may also require normalization.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, in March 2024 and March 2025, the Delaware Court of Chancery ruled that Mr. Jeffries was entitled to advancement by the Company of his defense costs for the civil litigation and for his defense costs for the criminal prosecution against him, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The advancement obligation is established, but the filings provide no separable amount, payment endpoint, reasonably possible range, or net insurance recovery. Existing legal costs and probable estimable liabilities are already expensed or accrued under the disclosed accounting policy; the finding concerns additional future amounts not presently measurable.
audit_findings.action: Monitor quarterly accruals and cash payments, obtain advancement invoices, insurance coverage and recoveries, reimbursement rights, and counsel's exposure estimate, and rerun only when a probable net claim or recurring normalized cost can be supported.
